rationale:
Decision: split into seven children: four reuses of comparator-accepted declarations with byte-identical frozen Lean types, and three new nodes. Conclusions (1) and (2) are elementary and are proved directly in this node's assembly.

Why split. The seven conjuncts have proofs of three different kinds.
 - Part I (transport under one dilation, (S0)–(S5)) gives (3), (4) and (6). Exactly these facts are already formalized and comparator-accepted in the density_and_tangent_cones branch, so they are reused, not re-proved: (S5) = dtc_blowUp_isMinimizingIn; (S2) and (S3) = dtc_blowUp_algebra (iii) and (iv); (S1) = dtc_blowUp_massOn_image.
 - Part II.4, the mass bound (5), is an analytic estimate for moving centres that combines the monotonicity hypothesis, (MR) and (S1): new child moving_mass_bound.
 - (7) consists of a differential-topology lemma, Part III (RET: a C¹ local retraction onto an embedded C² submanifold whose Lipschitz constants tend to 1; new child local_retraction), and its purely metric rescaling with the Case A/B disjunction, Part II.5–6 (new child moving_retractions). moving_retractions takes RET at x as a hypothesis, so it has no dependency and can be proved in parallel.
Each new child is a reusable statement about moving blow-ups or about submanifolds.

Proof-base plumbing. An implementation base in this run merges only a node's resolved dependencies and its children's commits, and a child's base contains only its own sibling dependencies. This node's only resolved dependency is mass_and_support. Hence:
 - The accepted Part I lemmas are listed as reused children: blowup_minimality = Submission.dtc_blowUp_isMinimizingIn (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.blowup_scaling-a1.minimality-a1, accepted, commit a8aa184); blowup_algebra = Submission.dtc_blowUp_algebra (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.blowup_scaling-a1.blowup_structure-a1, commit f64597f); blowup_mass_scaling = Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.blowup_scaling-a1.mass_scaling-a1, commit 17c63f2).

Its natural proof is copied from the grandparent's reviewed decomposition-v2, with two precision fixes in step 4.

If T is minimizing in A (IsMinimizingIn T A, Simon 7.1.1: T is integer multiplicity, and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) whenever W is open with closure W compact and contained in U, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary S T, and spt(S − T) is compact and contained in A ∩ W), then η_{x,λ#}T is minimizing in η(A). subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Part I, (S0)–(S5) and its direct form, of the selected node's supplied proof (Simon 7.1.1, chapter-07.txt lines 12–17; the dilation invariance used in the proof of 7.3.1, lines 317–337; Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 and 3.3–3.9). The declaration is already comparator-accepted (Lean proof at commit a8aa184); the argument it formalizes is the following.
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For V ⊆ ℝ^P and k ∈ ℕ, 𝒟ᵏ(V) = TestFormOn V k is the space of C^∞ k-forms ω on ℝ^P with compact tsupport ω ⊆ V (an element is determined by its underlying form), and 𝒟_k(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V k. |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors and, for Y ∈ 𝒟_k(V) and W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(Y) = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y} ∈ [0, ∞] (massOn). Fix x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0; η := dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), ι(z) := x + λz; for Y ∈ 𝒟_k(U), η_#Y := blowUp Y x λ ∈ 𝒟_k(η(U)).
1. (η is a similarity.) η is the linear homeomorphism y ↦ λ⁻¹y (λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) followed by the translation by −λ⁻¹x, so η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι: η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z and ι(η(y)) = x + λλ⁻¹(y − x) = y; |η(y) − η(y′)| = λ⁻¹|y − y′|. Hence η is bijective, η⁻¹(η(E)) = E, η(E ∩ F) = η(E) ∩ η(F), η⁻¹(closure E) = closure(η⁻¹(E)), η(closure E) = closure(η(E)), and η and ι = η⁻¹ map open sets to open sets and compact sets to compact sets. For continuous h and any f, tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f) (the closed set h⁻¹(tsupport f) contains {f∘h ≠ 0}); for the homeomorphism η this is an equality.
2. (Pull-backs and the test-form correspondence.) Unfolding blowUp (GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply, GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply; η⁻¹(η(U)) = U), η_#Y(ω) = Y(η^#ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)), where η^#ω is the affine pull-back affinePullbackForm (dilationCLM P λ) (−λ⁻¹x) ω regarded as an element of 𝒟ᵏ(U): (η^#ω)(y)(v₁, …, v_k) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁, …, λ⁻¹v_k) = λ^{−k}·ω(η(y))(v₁, …, v_k). So η^#ω = λ^{−k}(ω∘η), a smooth form with tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω), compact and contained in U. Conversely, for ω′ ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U) the form ω := λᵏ(ω′∘ι) is smooth with tsupport ω = η(tsupport ω′) compact ⊆ η(U), and η^#ω = ω′; ω is unique, since ω = λᵏ((η^#ω)∘ι). In particular, for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) the form ω∘η lies in 𝒟ᵏ(U) and η_#Y(ω) = λ^{−k}·Y(ω∘η) (linearity of Y); and for ω′ ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U) the form ω′∘ι lies in 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) and η_#Y(ω′∘ι) = λ^{−k}·Y(ω′).
3. (Mass scaling.) Let W ⊆ ℝ^P and Y ∈ 𝒟_k(U); call ω admissible for a current with domain V on a set W′ if ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ W′ and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. (a) If ω is admissible for η_#Y on η(W), then ω′ := ω∘η is admissible for Y on W (tsupport ω′ ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(W)) = W; |ω′(y)| = |ω(η(y))| ≤ 1), and ofReal(η_#Y(ω)) = ofReal(λ^{−k}Y(ω′)) = ofReal(λ^{−k})·ofReal(Y(ω′)) ≤ ofReal(λ^{−k})·M_W(Y) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, λ^{−k} ≥ 0); taking the supremum, M_{η(W)}(η_#Y) ≤ ofReal(λ^{−k})·M_W(Y). (b) If ω′ is admissible for Y on W, then ω := ω′∘ι is admissible for η_#Y on η(W) (tsupport ω ⊆ ι⁻¹(tsupport ω′) ⊆ ι⁻¹(W) = η(W); |ω(z)| = |ω′(ι(z))| ≤ 1) and ofReal(λ^{−k})·ofReal(Y(ω′)) = ofReal(η_#Y(ω)) ≤ M_{η(W)}(η_#Y); since multiplication by the finite constant ofReal(λ^{−k}) commutes with suprema in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.mul_sSup), ofReal(λ^{−k})·M_W(Y) ≤ M_{η(W)}(η_#Y). Hence M_{η(W)}(η_#Y) = ofReal(λ^{−k})·M_W(Y) = ofReal((λ⁻¹)ᵏ)·M_W(Y).
4. (Algebra.) Let S, Y ∈ 𝒟_k(U). (a) η_#(S − Y) = η_#S − η_#Y: for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) both sides equal S(η^#ω) − Y(η^#ω), the difference of currents being the pointwise difference of the linear functionals; currents agreeing on all test forms are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). (b) If η_#S = η_#Y then S = Y: every ω′ ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U) equals η^#ω for some ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) (step 2), so S(ω′) = η_#S(ω) = η_#Y(ω) = Y(ω′). (c) spt(η_#Y) = η(spt Y). Recall spt Z = V ∖ Z₀(Z) for a current Z with domain V, where the zero region Z₀(Z) is the union of the open W₀ with closure W₀ compact ⊆ V on which Z vanishes (Z(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W₀). If W₀ is open with closure W₀ compact ⊆ U and Y vanishes on W₀, then η(W₀) is open with closure η(closure W₀) compact ⊆ η(U), and η_#Y vanishes on η(W₀): if tsupport ω ⊆ η(W₀) then tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ W₀, so η_#Y(ω) = Y(η^#ω) = 0. Conversely, if W₀′ is open with closure W₀′ compact ⊆ η(U) and η_#Y vanishes on W₀′, then W₀ := η⁻¹(W₀′) is open with closure η⁻¹(closure W₀′) compact ⊆ U, and Y vanishes on W₀: if tsupport ω′ ⊆ W₀, write ω′ = η^#ω with ω = λᵏ(ω′∘ι), tsupport ω = η(tsupport ω′) ⊆ W₀′, so Y(ω′) = η_#Y(ω) = 0. Hence Z₀(η_#Y) = η(Z₀(Y)), and spt(η_#Y) = η(U) ∖ η(Z₀(Y)) = η(U ∖ Z₀(Y)) = η(spt Y) because η is injective. (d) If k = m + 1 and β ∈ 𝒟^m(η(U)), then ∂(η_#Y)(β) = η_#Y(dβ) = Y(η^#(dβ)) = Y(d(η^#β)) = ∂Y(η^#β) = η_#(∂Y)(β), because exterior differentiation commutes with affine pull-back (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm; at the level of currents GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward, restricting the domain commuting with ∂). Hence ∂(η_#Y) = η_#(∂Y).
5. (The inverse push-forward.) For X ∈ 𝒟_k(η(U)) define X^♭(ω′) := X(λᵏ(ω′∘ι)) for ω′ ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U). The map ω′ ↦ λᵏ(ω′∘ι) is linear from 𝒟ᵏ(U) to 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) (step 2) and sequentially continuous: if ω′_i → ω′ in 𝒟ᵏ(U) (supports in one compact K ⊆ U, all derivatives converging uniformly), the forms λᵏ(ω′_i∘ι) have supports in the compact set η(K) ⊆ η(U), and by the chain rule for the affine map ι their j-th derivatives are the j-th derivatives of ω′_i at ι(·) with every argument multiplied by λ, so they converge uniformly as well. Hence X^♭ ∈ 𝒟_k(U). By step 2, η_#(X^♭)(ω) = X^♭(η^#ω) = X(λᵏ((λ^{−k}(ω∘η))∘ι)) = X(ω), i.e. η_#(X^♭) = X. (X^♭ is the push-forward of X by the similarity ι = dilation(−λ⁻¹x, λ⁻¹), which maps η(U) onto U, with pull-back ι^#ω′ = λᵏ(ω′∘ι); so everything proved here for η also holds for ι, with λ replaced by λ⁻¹ and U by η(U).)
6. (Integer multiplicity is preserved.) Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Then R′ := (η(M), θ∘ι, ξ∘ι) is an IMRep of η_#Y in η(U): (a) Hⁿ(η(E)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P, because η is the scaling by λ⁻¹ followed by a translation, Hⁿ = μHE[n] is translation invariant, and Hⁿ(cE) = cⁿHⁿ(E) for c > 0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀; cf. the accepted dtc_hausdorff_dilation); equivalently η_*(Hⁿ) = λⁿHⁿ (Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) = Hⁿ(ι(B)) = λⁿHⁿ(B)); hence ∫_{η(E)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_E g∘η dHⁿ for Borel E and Borel g that is ≥ 0 or integrable. (b) η(M) ⊆ η(U) is Borel (image of a Borel set under a homeomorphism) and countably n-rectifiable: if M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_i F_i(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz, then η(M) ⊆ η(M₀) ∪ ⋃_i (η∘F_i)(ℝⁿ), each η∘F_i is Lipschitz, and Hⁿ(η(M₀)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(M₀) = 0. (c) θ∘ι is measurable, ℕ-valued and ≥ 1 on η(M); for compact K ⊆ η(U), ι(K) ⊆ U is compact and ∫_{η(M)∩K} θ∘ι dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_{M∩ι(K)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by (a) and the local integrability of θ. (d) ξ∘ι is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞η(M): η is a measurable equivalence with η_*(Hⁿ⌞M) = λⁿ·Hⁿ⌞η(M) by (a), and composition with η⁻¹ = ι transports a.e. strong measurability. (e) Orientation: let y ∈ M be such that ξ(y) = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of an approximate tangent space Q of M at y (true for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M), and z := η(y). For ρ > 0, η_{z,ρ}(η(w)) = (η(w) − z)/ρ = (w − y)/(λρ) = η_{y,λρ}(w), so η_{z,ρ}(η(M)) = η_{y,λρ}(M) and ∫_{η_{z,ρ}(η(M))} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{y,λρ}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as ρ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P): HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n η(M) z Q (cf. the accepted dtc_approxTangent_dilation), and (ξ∘ι)(z) = ξ(y) orients Q. subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Part I, (S0)(ii), (S2) and (S3), of the selected node's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 and 2.23–2.24(1): ∂f_#T = f_#∂T, chapter-06.txt lines 405–418). The declaration is already comparator-accepted (Lean proof at commit f64597f); the argument it formalizes is the following.
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For V ⊆ ℝ^P and k ∈ ℕ, 𝒟ᵏ(V) = TestFormOn V k is the space of C^∞ k-forms ω on ℝ^P with compact tsupport ω ⊆ V (an element is determined by its underlying form), and 𝒟_k(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V k. |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors and, for Y ∈ 𝒟_k(V) and W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(Y) = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y} ∈ [0, ∞] (massOn). Fix x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0; η := dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), ι(z) := x + λz; for Y ∈ 𝒟_k(U), η_#Y := blowUp Y x λ ∈ 𝒟_k(η(U)).
1. (η is a similarity.) η is the linear homeomorphism y ↦ λ⁻¹y (λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) followed by the translation by −λ⁻¹x, so η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι: η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z and ι(η(y)) = x + λλ⁻¹(y − x) = y; |η(y) − η(y′)| = λ⁻¹|y − y′|. Hence η is bijective, η⁻¹(η(E)) = E, η(E ∩ F) = η(E) ∩ η(F), η⁻¹(closure E) = closure(η⁻¹(E)), η(closure E) = closure(η(E)), and η and ι = η⁻¹ map open sets to open sets and compact sets to compact sets. For continuous h and any f, tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f) (the closed set h⁻¹(tsupport f) contains {f∘h ≠ 0}); for the homeomorphism η this is an equality.
2. (Pull-backs and the test-form correspondence.) Unfolding blowUp (GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply, GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply; η⁻¹(η(U)) = U), η_#Y(ω) = Y(η^#ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)), where η^#ω is the affine pull-back affinePullbackForm (dilationCLM P λ) (−λ⁻¹x) ω regarded as an element of 𝒟ᵏ(U): (η^#ω)(y)(v₁, …, v_k) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁, …, λ⁻¹v_k) = λ^{−k}·ω(η(y))(v₁, …, v_k). So η^#ω = λ^{−k}(ω∘η), a smooth form with tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω), compact and contained in U. Conversely, for ω′ ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U) the form ω := λᵏ(ω′∘ι) is smooth with tsupport ω = η(tsupport ω′) compact ⊆ η(U), and η^#ω = ω′; ω is unique, since ω = λᵏ((η^#ω)∘ι). In particular, for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) the form ω∘η lies in 𝒟ᵏ(U) and η_#Y(ω) = λ^{−k}·Y(ω∘η) (linearity of Y); and for ω′ ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U) the form ω′∘ι lies in 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) and η_#Y(ω′∘ι) = λ^{−k}·Y(ω′).
3. (Algebra.) Let S, Y ∈ 𝒟_k(U). (a) η_#(S − Y) = η_#S − η_#Y: for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) both sides equal S(η^#ω) − Y(η^#ω), the difference of currents being the pointwise difference of the linear functionals; currents agreeing on all test forms are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). (b) If η_#S = η_#Y then S = Y: every ω′ ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U) equals η^#ω for some ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)) (step 2), so S(ω′) = η_#S(ω) = η_#Y(ω) = Y(ω′). (c) spt(η_#Y) = η(spt Y). Recall spt Z = V ∖ Z₀(Z) for a current Z with domain V, where the zero region Z₀(Z) is the union of the open W₀ with closure W₀ compact ⊆ V on which Z vanishes (Z(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W₀). If W₀ is open with closure W₀ compact ⊆ U and Y vanishes on W₀, then η(W₀) is open with closure η(closure W₀) compact ⊆ η(U), and η_#Y vanishes on η(W₀): if tsupport ω ⊆ η(W₀) then tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ W₀, so η_#Y(ω) = Y(η^#ω) = 0. Conversely, if W₀′ is open with closure W₀′ compact ⊆ η(U) and η_#Y vanishes on W₀′, then W₀ := η⁻¹(W₀′) is open with closure η⁻¹(closure W₀′) compact ⊆ U, and Y vanishes on W₀: if tsupport ω′ ⊆ W₀, write ω′ = η^#ω with ω = λᵏ(ω′∘ι), tsupport ω = η(tsupport ω′) ⊆ W₀′, so Y(ω′) = η_#Y(ω) = 0. Hence Z₀(η_#Y) = η(Z₀(Y)), and spt(η_#Y) = η(U) ∖ η(Z₀(Y)) = η(U ∖ Z₀(Y)) = η(spt Y) because η is injective. (d) If k = m + 1 and β ∈ 𝒟^m(η(U)), then ∂(η_#Y)(β) = η_#Y(dβ) = Y(η^#(dβ)) = Y(d(η^#β)) = ∂Y(η^#β) = η_#(∂Y)(β), because exterior differentiation commutes with affine pull-back (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm; at the level of currents GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward, restricting the domain commuting with ∂). Hence ∂(η_#Y) = η_#(∂Y).
4. (Conclusion.) Step 3(a) is (i), step 3(b) is (ii) (for every degree n), step 3(c) is (iii) and step 3(d) is (iv). No hypothesis on U was used. ∎
proof_key_steps: blowUp evaluates on the affine pull-back η^#ω = λ^{−k}(ω∘η), and every test form in U is such a pull-back (inverse λᵏ(ω′∘ι)).
(i) both sides evaluate S − T on η^#ω; (ii) injectivity from surjectivity of the pull-back and λ^{−k} ≠ 0.
(iii) zero regions correspond under η: Z(η_#T) = η(Z(T)), so spt(η_#T) = η(spt T).
(iv) d commutes with affine pull-back (exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm / boundary_affinePushforward).

2. (Pull-backs and the test-form correspondence.) Unfolding blowUp (GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply, GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply; η⁻¹(η(U)) = U), η_#Y(ω) = Y(η^#ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(η(U)), where η^#ω is the affine pull-back affinePullbackForm (dilationCLM P λ) (−λ⁻¹x) ω regarded as an element of 𝒟ᵏ(U): (η^#ω)(y)(v₁, …, v_k) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁, …, λ⁻¹v_k) = λ^{−k}·ω(η(y))(v₁, …, v_k). subproblems.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12) — reused accepted declaration
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3), 2.11–2.12. Notation: μ := μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (covectorEuclideanNorm; I strictly increasing multi-indices), dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}, ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ := ξ(x)(α).
1. Where R.orients holds at x ∈ M (Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so μ-a.e.), ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = s·Σ_I α(e_I)det(τ^I) with τ orthonormal, s = ±1 (multilinearity, alternation; τ^I = rows I of the matrix of τ), and Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1 (Cauchy–Binet). So |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Schwarz), and ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), so |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ (n = 0: I = ∅, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1). ξ^♭ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous linear in ξ; R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: a.e. strongly measurable, zero off the compact spt ω ⊆ U, a.e. bounded by θ·sup|ω| (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). So T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩dμ.
3. For open W and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), ⟨ω, ξ⟩ ≤ 1 μ-a.e. (step 1) and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ(W) (step 2). So M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. For real t < μ(W) (μ(W) = ∞ allowed) we find admissible ω with T(ω) > t. G := W ∩ U is open and σ-compact, μ(G) = μ(W) (M ⊆ U), and μ, finite on compacts of U, is Radon on G (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15): inner regular by compacts, outer regular on finite-measure sets. Choose a compact K ⊆ G with μ(K) > t (inner regularity; μ(K) < ∞ as K is a compact subset of U), then η > 0 with μ(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon 1.17) and inner regularity: a compact K' ⊆ K ∩ E₁, where E₁ is a Borel set of full μ-measure on which |ξ^♭| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ (step 1), with μ(K ∖ K') < η and ξ^♭|K' continuous. (b) An open V ⊇ K' with V̄ ⊆ G compact, μ(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend ξ^♭|K' coefficientwise continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), retract radially onto the closed |·|-unit ball of Λⁿ(ℝ^P), multiply by a continuous χ: ℝ^P → [0, 1], χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V: g is continuous, spt g ⊆ V compact, |g| ≤ 1, g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise, standard mollifier): for 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V) it is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)|dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_ε → g uniformly; so g_ε is admissible. (e) With δ_ε := sup|g_ε − g|·μ(V̄) → 0 (μ(V̄) < ∞), steps 2, 1 give T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩dμ ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩dμ − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩|dμ − δ_ε ≥ μ(K') − η − δ_ε ≥ μ(K) − 2η − δ_ε > t + 2η − δ_ε > t for small ε. With step 3 this is (i).
5. spt T = U ∖ Z (GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11), Z the union of the open W with W̄ ⊆ U compact and T(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ W; x ∈ spt μ iff μ(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ lay in such a W, then M_W(T) = 0, so μ(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ; so U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ, take r > 0 with μ(B_r(x)) = 0, B̄_r(x) ⊆ U; by step 2 T(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), so x ∈ Z, x ∉ spt T. Hence (ii).
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., and ξ^♭ satisfies |ξ^♭| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩.
Integral formula T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
Upper bound: admissible ω give T(ω) ≤ μ(W), so M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
Lower bound: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, cutoff and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) > t for each real t < μ(W).
Support: by (i) and the integral formula, the zero region Z of T is U ∖ spt μ, so spt T = U ∩ spt μ.

subproblems.title: Locally bounded masses of blow-ups at moving centres, from the monotonicity inequality
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) an integer multiplicity current (IsIntegerMultiplicity T). Assume: for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ ≥ 0 such that for all y ∈ ℝ^P and R ∈ ℝ with closedBall(y, R) ⊆ K the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (values in [0, ∞]) is monotone on (0, R). Let x ∈ U, x_j ∈ ℝ^P with x_j → x, and λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0. Then for every R ∈ ℝ there is c ∈ [0, ∞) (c ≠ ∞) such that M_{B_R(0)}(blowUp T x_j λ_j) ≤ c for all large j (eventually in atTop), where B_R(0) = ball 0 R and blowUp T x_j λ_j = η_{x_j,λ_j#}T ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{x_j,λ_j}(U)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ Λ : ℝ, 0 ≤ Λ ∧ ∀ (y : Euclid P) (R : ℝ), closedBall y R ⊆ K → MonotoneOn (fun ρ : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * ρ) / ρ ^ n) * T.massOn (ball y ρ)) (Ioo 0 R)) → ∀ (x : Euclid P) (xs : ℕ → Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (hlams : ∀ j, 0 < lams j), x ∈ U → Tendsto xs atTop (𝓝 x) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ c : ℝ≥0∞, c ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, (blowUp T (xs j) (lams j) (hlams j).ne').massOn (ball 0 R) ≤ c

Source: Part II.4 of the selected node's supplied proof (Simon 7.3.1, proof, chapter-07.txt lines 325–331: the scaling identity (ωₙRⁿ)⁻¹M_{B_R(0)}(η_{x,λ_j#}T) = (ωₙλ_jⁿRⁿ)⁻¹M_{B_{λ_jR}(x)}(T) together with the monotonicity formula gives sup_j M_{B_R(0)}(η_{x,λ_j#}T) < ∞; here the centres x_j move). Dependencies (siblings): mass_and_support = Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (MR: for U open and an IMRep R₀ representing T, M_W(T) = R₀.measure(W) for every open W) and blowup_mass_scaling = Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image (MS: for λ > 0 and every W, M_{η_{a,λ}(W)}(blowUp T a λ) = ofReal((λ⁻¹)ⁿ)·M_W(T)).
Notation: λ_j := lams j > 0, x_j := xs j, η_j := dilation x_j λ_j (η_j(y) = λ_j⁻¹(y − x_j)), S_j := blowUp T x_j λ_j, B_s(y) := ball y s; 'for all large j' means eventually in atTop.
1. (Radius.) U is open and x ∈ U, so there is ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ U; put r := ε/3 > 0. Then K := closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ U, and K is compact (closed balls of ℝ^P are compact).
2. (Monotonicity.) The hypothesis applied to K gives Λ ≥ 0 such that for all y ∈ ℝ^P and s ∈ ℝ with closedBall(y, s) ⊆ K, the function f_y(ρ) := ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ∈ [0, ∞] is monotone (nondecreasing) on (0, s).
3. (Finite mass near x.) T is integer multiplicity; let R₀ = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep representing T in U. By MR (U and B_{2r}(x) open), M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) = R₀.measure(B_{2r}(x)) ≤ R₀.measure(K) (B_{2r}(x) ⊆ K). By definition R₀.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, so, K being Borel, R₀.measure(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict), which is finite by the local integrability of θ (R₀.locallyIntegrable_mult, K compact ⊆ U). Hence M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) < ∞ and c₁ := ofReal(e^{Λr}(2/r)ⁿ)·M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) is finite.
4. (Uniform density bound near x.) Claim: if |y − x| < r and 0 < ρ < r/2, then M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·c₁. (a) closedBall(y, r) ⊆ K, since |z − y| ≤ r gives |z − x| ≤ |z − y| + |y − x| < 2r. By step 2 with s := r, f_y is monotone on (0, r); as ρ and r/2 lie in (0, r) and ρ ≤ r/2, f_y(ρ) ≤ f_y(r/2) = ofReal(e^{Λr/2}/(r/2)ⁿ)·M_{B_{r/2}(y)}(T). (b) B_{r/2}(y) ⊆ B_{2r}(x) (|z − x| < r/2 + r), so M_{B_{r/2}(y)}(T) ≤ M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) (massOn is monotone in the set, GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono); and e^{Λr/2}/(r/2)ⁿ = e^{Λr/2}(2/r)ⁿ ≤ e^{Λr}(2/r)ⁿ since Λ ≥ 0 and r > 0. Hence f_y(r/2) ≤ c₁. (c) Since Λρ ≥ 0, e^{Λρ} ≥ 1, so ρ^{−n} ≤ e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ and ofReal(ρ^{−n})·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ f_y(ρ) ≤ c₁. Multiplying by ofReal(ρⁿ) and using ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal(ρ^{−n}) = ofReal(1) = 1 (ρ > 0) gives M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·c₁.
5. (The constant.) Let R ∈ ℝ, put R′ := max(R, 1) > 0 and c := ofReal(R′ⁿ)·c₁, which is finite. (Using R′ instead of R also covers R ≤ 0, where alternatively B_R(0) = ∅ and M_∅ = 0.)
6. (Large j.) Since x_j → x and λ_jR′ → 0·R′ = 0, for all large j both |x_j − x| < r and λ_jR′ < r/2 hold. Fix such j. (a) η_j(B_{λ_jR′}(x_j)) = B_{R′}(0): if |y − x_j| < λ_jR′ then |η_j(y)| = λ_j⁻¹|y − x_j| < R′; conversely, for |z| < R′ the point y := x_j + λ_jz satisfies |y − x_j| = λ_j|z| < λ_jR′ and η_j(y) = λ_j⁻¹(λ_jz) = z. (b) Since B_R(0) ⊆ B_{R′}(0), monotonicity of massOn, MS with W := B_{λ_jR′}(x_j), and step 4 with y := x_j and ρ := λ_jR′ ∈ (0, r/2) give M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ M_{B_{R′}(0)}(S_j) = M_{η_j(W)}(S_j) = ofReal((λ_j⁻¹)ⁿ)·M_W(T) ≤ ofReal((λ_j⁻¹)ⁿ)·ofReal((λ_jR′)ⁿ)·c₁ = ofReal((λ_j⁻¹)ⁿ(λ_jR′)ⁿ)·c₁ = ofReal(R′ⁿ)·c₁ = c.
7. (Conclusion.) For every R ∈ ℝ, c ≠ ∞ and M_{B_R(0)}(blowUp T x_j λ_j) ≤ c for all large j. Minimality was not used, and for n = 0 all powers equal 1 and the argument is unchanged. ∎

theorem Submission.dimred_mbl_bh_moving_blowUp_mass_bound : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ Λ : ℝ, 0 ≤ Λ ∧ ∀ (y : Euclid P) (R : ℝ), closedBall y R ⊆ K → MonotoneOn (fun ρ : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * ρ) / ρ ^ n) * T.massOn (ball y ρ)) (Ioo 0 R)) → ∀ (x : Euclid P) (xs : ℕ → Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (hlams : ∀ j, 0 < lams j), x ∈ U → Tendsto xs atTop (𝓝 x) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ c : ℝ≥0∞, c ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, (blowUp T (xs j) (lams j) (hlams j).ne').massOn (ball 0 R) ≤ c := by
  intro P n U T hU hIM hmon x xs lams hlams hxU hxs hlam0 R
  -- `η_{a,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹ • (y - a)`
  have hdil : ∀ (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (y : Euclid P), dilation a lam y = lam⁻¹ • (y - a) := by
    intro a lam y
    simp only [dilation, dilationCLM, FunLike.coe_smul, Pi.smul_apply,
      ContinuousLinearMap.coe_id', id_eq, smul_sub]
    abel
  -- Step 0: a radius `r` with `closedBall x (2r) ⊆ U`
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hεU⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.1 hU x hxU
  set r := ε / 3 with hr_def
  have hr : 0 < r := by positivity
  have hK : closedBall x (2 * r) ⊆ U := by
    intro y hy
    apply hεU
    rw [mem_ball]
    rw [mem_closedBall] at hy
    linarith
  have hKc : IsCompact (closedBall x (2 * r)) := isCompact_closedBall x (2 * r)
  -- Step 1: monotonicity on `K = closedBall x (2r)`
  obtain ⟨Λ, hΛ, hmono⟩ := hmon _ hKc hK
  -- Step 2: `M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) < ∞`
  obtain ⟨Rep, hRep⟩ := hIM
  have hfin : T.massOn (ball x (2 * r)) ≠ ∞ := by
    rw [(Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support P n U T Rep hU hRep).1 _ isOpen_ball]
    have h1 : Rep.measure (ball x (2 * r)) ≤ Rep.measure (closedBall x (2 * r)) :=
      measure_mono ball_subset_closedBall
    have h2 : Rep.measure (closedBall x (2 * r)) =
        ∫⁻ y in Rep.carrier ∩ closedBall x (2 * r), (Rep.mult y : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n] := by
      unfold IMRep.measure
      rw [withDensity_apply _ measurableSet_closedBall,
        Measure.restrict_restrict measurableSet_closedBall, inter_comm]
    have h3 := Rep.locallyIntegrable_mult _ hKc hK
    rw [← h2] at h3
    exact ne_top_of_le_ne_top h3 h1
  -- Step 3: the constant `c₁`
  set c₁ : ℝ≥0∞ := ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * r) * (2 / r) ^ n) * T.massOn (ball x (2 * r))
    with hc₁_def
  have hc₁ : c₁ ≠ ∞ := ENNReal.mul_ne_top ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top hfin
  -- Step 4: `M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ρⁿ c₁` for `|y - x| < r`, `0 < ρ < r/2`
  have hkey : ∀ y : Euclid P, dist y x < r → ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < r / 2 →
      T.massOn (ball y ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) * c₁ := by
    intro y hy ρ hρ hρr
    have hKy : closedBall y r ⊆ closedBall x (2 * r) := by
      intro z hz
      rw [mem_closedBall] at hz ⊢
      linarith [dist_triangle z y x]
    have hρmem : ρ ∈ Ioo 0 r := ⟨hρ, by linarith⟩
    have hr2mem : r / 2 ∈ Ioo 0 r := ⟨by positivity, by linarith⟩
    have hle := hmono y r hKy hρmem hr2mem hρr.le
    have hball : ball y (r / 2) ⊆ ball x (2 * r) := by
      intro z hz
      rw [mem_ball] at hz ⊢
      linarith [dist_triangle z y x]
    have hM : T.massOn (ball y (r / 2)) ≤ T.massOn (ball x (2 * r)) := T.massOn_mono hball
    have hcoef : ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * (r / 2)) / (r / 2) ^ n) ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * r) * (2 / r) ^ n) := by
      apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
      rw [div_eq_mul_inv, ← inv_pow, inv_div]
      gcongr
      nlinarith
    have h1 : ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * ρ) / ρ ^ n) * T.massOn (ball y ρ) ≤ c₁ :=
      hle.trans (mul_le_mul' hcoef hM)
    have hexp : 1 ≤ Real.exp (Λ * ρ) := Real.one_le_exp (by positivity)
    have h2 : ENNReal.ofReal ((ρ ^ n)⁻¹) * T.massOn (ball y ρ) ≤ c₁ := by
      refine le_trans (mul_le_mul' (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal ?_) le_rfl) h1
      rw [div_eq_mul_inv]
      have : 0 < (ρ ^ n)⁻¹ := by positivity
      nlinarith
    calc T.massOn (ball y ρ)
        = ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) * (ENNReal.ofReal ((ρ ^ n)⁻¹) * T.massOn (ball y ρ)) := by
          rw [← mul_assoc, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity),
            mul_inv_cancel₀ (by positivity), ENNReal.ofReal_one, one_mul]
      _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) * c₁ := mul_le_mul' le_rfl h2
  -- Step 5: rescale
  set R' := max R 1 with hR'_def
  have hR' : 0 < R' := lt_of_lt_of_le one_pos (le_max_right _ _)
  refine ⟨ENNReal.ofReal (R' ^ n) * c₁, ENNReal.mul_ne_top ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top hc₁, ?_⟩
  have hev1 : ∀ᶠ j in atTop, dist (xs j) x < r := Metric.tendsto_nhds.1 hxs r hr
  have hev2 : ∀ᶠ j in atTop, lams j * R' < r / 2 := by
    have h0 : Tendsto (fun j => lams j * R') atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      simpa using hlam0.mul_const R'
    exact (tendsto_order.1 h0).2 (r / 2) (by positivity)
  filter_upwards [hev1, hev2] with j hj1 hj2
  have hlam := hlams j
  have himg : dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' ball (xs j) (lams j * R') = ball 0 R' := by
    ext z
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
      rw [mem_ball, dist_zero_right, hdil, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (inv_nonneg.2 hlam.le),
        ← dist_eq_norm]
      rw [mem_ball] at hy
      calc (lams j)⁻¹ * dist y (xs j) < (lams j)⁻¹ * (lams j * R') :=
            mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hy (inv_pos.2 hlam)
        _ = R' := by field_simp
    · intro hz
      refine ⟨xs j + lams j • z, ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [mem_ball, dist_eq_norm, add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg hlam.le]
        rw [mem_ball, dist_zero_right] at hz
        exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hz hlam
      · rw [hdil, add_sub_cancel_left, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hlam.ne', one_smul]
  calc (blowUp T (xs j) (lams j) (hlams j).ne').massOn (ball 0 R)
      ≤ (blowUp T (xs j) (lams j) (hlams j).ne').massOn (ball 0 R') :=
        GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono _ (ball_subset_ball (le_max_left _ _))
    _ = (blowUp T (xs j) (lams j) (hlams j).ne').massOn
          (dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' ball (xs j) (lams j * R')) := by rw [himg]
    _ = ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j)⁻¹ ^ n) * T.massOn (ball (xs j) (lams j * R')) :=
        Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image P n U T (xs j) (lams j) (hlams j) _
    _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j)⁻¹ ^ n) * (ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j * R') ^ n) * c₁) :=
        mul_le_mul' le_rfl (hkey _ hj1 _ (by positivity) hj2)
    _ = ENNReal.ofReal (R' ^ n) * c₁ := by
        rw [← mul_assoc, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity), ← mul_pow,
          inv_mul_cancel_left₀ hlam.ne']
proof_key_steps: Fix r with closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ U; the monotonicity hypothesis on K = closedBall(x, 2r) gives Λ ≥ 0.
MR and the local integrability of the multiplicity give M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T) < ∞, hence the finite constant c₁ = ofReal(e^{Λr}(2/r)ⁿ)M_{B_{2r}(x)}(T).
Monotonicity between ρ and r/2 on balls centred at y with |y − x| < r gives M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)c₁ for 0 < ρ < r/2.
For large j, η_j(B_{λ_jR′}(x_j)) = B_{R′}(0), and mass scaling gives M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ ofReal(λ_j^{−n})ofReal((λ_jR′)ⁿ)c₁ = ofReal(R′ⁿ)c₁ with R′ = max(R, 1).

subproblems.title: Local C¹ retraction onto an embedded C² submanifold with Lipschitz constants tending to 1
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N: every y ∈ N has an open W ∋ y and a map ψ, C² and injective on an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, with ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ injective on V), and x ∈ N. Then there are δ > 0 and π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that (i) π is C¹ on B_δ(x) = ball x δ; (ii) π maps B_δ(x) into N; (iii) π(y) = y for every y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x); (iv) for every η > 0 there is s with 0 < s ≤ δ and |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_s(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → x ∈ N → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (π : Euclid P → Euclid P), 0 < δ ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 π (ball x δ) ∧ MapsTo π (ball x δ) N ∧ (∀ y ∈ N ∩ ball x δ, π y = y) ∧ ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ s ≤ δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ ball x s, ∀ z ∈ ball x s, ‖π y - π z‖ ≤ (1 + η) * ‖y - z‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Part III (RET) of the selected node's supplied proof. It replaces the nearest-point projection onto N used for the compactness theorem with constraint (Simon 7.2.5(2), chapter-07.txt lines 166–174) by an explicit graph retraction, which agrees with the nearest-point projection to first order at x; embedded submanifolds are as in Simon Ch. 2, §4 (4.1) (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold). No dependencies. Mathlib tools: the inverse function theorem (ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, ContDiffAt.localInverse, ContDiffAt.to_localInverse, OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm), orthogonal projections (Submodule.starProjection, Submodule.starProjection_norm_le), LinearEquiv.ofInjective, and the mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le).
Notation: B_s(y) := ball y s ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P; B^d_s(0) := ball 0 s ⊆ ℝ^d = Euclid d; Df(v) := fderiv ℝ f v; ‖·‖ the operator norm.
1. (Chart at x.) Since x ∈ N, IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N gives an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, an open W ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ W, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P which is C² on V and injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(v) injective for every v ∈ V. As x ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V), choose v₀ ∈ V with ψ(v₀) = x. Since V is open and ψ is C² on V, ψ is differentiable at every point of V and Dψ is continuous on V. Put L := Dψ(v₀) : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, an injective continuous linear map; Q := L(ℝ^d), a (closed, finite-dimensional) subspace; L₀ : ℝ^d ≅ Q the linear isomorphism induced by L (LinearEquiv.ofInjective), continuous in finite dimension. Let p : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be the orthogonal projection onto Q (Q.starProjection): p is continuous linear, ‖p‖ ≤ 1, and p(q) = q for q ∈ Q. Define A := L₀⁻¹∘p : ℝ^P → ℝ^d (continuous linear; p regarded with values in Q). Then A(Lw) = L₀⁻¹(Lw) = w for w ∈ ℝ^d, i.e. A∘L = id, and L∘A = p.
2. (Local inverse.) Define h : ℝ^d → ℝ^d, h(v) := A(ψ(v) − x). Then h is C² on V (ψ followed by an affine map), h(v₀) = A(0) = 0, and Dh(v₀) = A∘Dψ(v₀) = A∘L = id. By the inverse function theorem there is an open set V₀ with v₀ ∈ V₀ ⊆ V such that O := h(V₀) is open, h maps V₀ bijectively onto O, and the inverse k : O → V₀ is C¹ on O with Dk(h(v)) = Dh(v)⁻¹ (shrinking V₀ we may assume Dh(v) is invertible for every v ∈ V₀, invertibility being an open condition and Dh continuous; then OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm shows that k is C¹ at every point of O). Thus k(h(v)) = v for v ∈ V₀, k(u) ∈ V₀ and h(k(u)) = u for u ∈ O, 0 = h(v₀) ∈ O, k(0) = v₀ and Dk(0) = Dh(v₀)⁻¹ = id.
3. (Graph parametrization.) Φ := ψ∘k : O → ℝ^P is C¹ on O (k is C¹ on O with values in V₀ ⊆ V, where ψ is C²); Φ(0) = ψ(v₀) = x; Φ(O) = ψ(k(O)) = ψ(V₀) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N; and DΦ(0) = Dψ(v₀)∘Dk(0) = L∘id = L.
4. (ψ(V₀) is relatively open in N.) Let F := V ∖ V₀. Claim: if y ∈ W and y = lim_i ψ(f_i) with all f_i ∈ F, then y ∈ ψ(F). Indeed K := {y} ∪ {ψ(f_i) : i ∈ ℕ} is compact (a convergent sequence together with its limit) and K ⊆ W (ψ(f_i) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ W), so all f_i lie in the compact set V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K), and a subsequence f_{i_l} converges to some f ∈ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K). As f_{i_l} ∉ V₀ and V₀ is open, f ∉ V₀, so f ∈ F; ψ is continuous at f ∈ V (V open), so ψ(f) = lim ψ(f_{i_l}) = y. Hence W ∩ closure(ψ(F)) = ψ(F) (recall ψ(F) ⊆ W), and W₀ := W ∖ ψ(F) = W ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ closure ψ(F)) is open. x ∈ W₀: x ∈ W, and if x = ψ(f) with f ∈ F ⊆ V then f = v₀ by injectivity of ψ on V, contradicting v₀ ∈ V₀. Finally W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V₀): if y ∈ W₀ ∩ N ⊆ W ∩ N = ψ(V), then y = ψ(v) with v ∈ V and v ∉ F (otherwise y ∈ ψ(F)), so v ∈ V₀; conversely ψ(V₀) ⊆ ψ(V) = W ∩ N, and ψ(V₀) ∩ ψ(F) = ∅ by injectivity of ψ on V (V₀ ∩ F = ∅).
5. (Choice of δ and π.) O is open and 0 ∈ O: choose r₀ > 0 with B^d_{r₀}(0) ⊆ O. W₀ is open and x ∈ W₀: choose δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ W₀ and ‖A‖·δ < r₀ (e.g. also δ < r₀/(‖A‖ + 1)). Define π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P by π(y) := Φ(A(y − x)) for y ∈ B_δ(x) and π(y) := y otherwise. For y ∈ B_δ(x), |A(y − x)| ≤ ‖A‖·|y − x| ≤ ‖A‖·δ < r₀, so A(y − x) ∈ B^d_{r₀}(0) ⊆ O.
6. ((i)–(iii).) (i) On the open ball B_δ(x), π coincides with Φ∘a, where a(y) := A(y − x) is affine (C^∞) and maps B_δ(x) into O, on which Φ is C¹; hence π is C¹ on B_δ(x) (ContDiffOn.comp, ContDiffOn.congr). (ii) For y ∈ B_δ(x), π(y) = Φ(A(y − x)) ∈ Φ(O) ⊆ N, so π maps B_δ(x) into N. (iii) If y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x), then y ∈ N ∩ W₀ = ψ(V₀) by step 4, so y = ψ(v) with v ∈ V₀; then A(y − x) = h(v) ∈ O and π(y) = ψ(k(h(v))) = ψ(v) = y. In particular π(x) = x.
7. ((iv).) π is C¹ on the open set B_δ(x), so π is differentiable at every y ∈ B_δ(x) and Dπ is continuous on B_δ(x) (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). By the chain rule (π = Φ∘a on a neighbourhood of y), Dπ(y) = DΦ(A(y − x))∘A for y ∈ B_δ(x); hence Dπ(x) = DΦ(0)∘A = L∘A = p and ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1. Let η > 0. By continuity of Dπ at x there is s with 0 < s ≤ δ and ‖Dπ(y) − Dπ(x)‖ ≤ η for all y ∈ B_s(x); then ‖Dπ(y)‖ ≤ ‖Dπ(x)‖ + η ≤ 1 + η on B_s(x). The ball B_s(x) is convex and π is differentiable on it, so the mean value inequality gives |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_s(x).
8. (Conclusion.) δ > 0 and π satisfy: π is C¹ on B_δ(x) (step 6(i)); π maps B_δ(x) into N (step 6(ii)); π(y) = y for y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x) (step 6(iii)); and for every η > 0 there is s ∈ (0, δ] such that |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_s(x) (step 7). The case d = 0 is included: ℝ⁰ is a point, L = 0 is injective, Q = {0}, p = 0, A = 0, Φ ≡ x, π ≡ x on B_δ(x), and N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ ψ(V₀) = {x} by step 4. ∎

The inverse function theorem for h := A(ψ − x) at v₀ gives V₀ ∋ v₀, O = h(V₀) ∋ 0 and a C¹ inverse k; Φ := ψ∘k parametrizes ψ(V₀) ⊆ N with DΦ(0) = L.

subproblems.title: Rescaled retractions onto the blown-up constraint sets η_{x_j,λ_j}(U ∩ N) at moving centres
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, N ⊆ ℝ^P with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and x ∈ U. Assume that if x ∈ N there are δ > 0 and π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with π C¹ on B_δ(x), π(B_δ(x)) ⊆ N, π(y) = y for y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x), and for every η > 0 some s ∈ (0, δ] with |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for y, z ∈ B_s(x). Let x_j ∈ ℝ^P with x_j → x and λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0, and A_j := η_{x_j,λ_j}(U ∩ N) (η_{x_j,λ_j} = dilation x_j λ_j). Then for every G > 0 there are maps π_j : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) and G′ ∈ ℝ such that: for all large j, either A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅, or π_j is C¹ on B_G(0), maps B_G(0) into A_j ∩ B_{G′}(0) and π_j(y) = y for y ∈ A_j ∩ B_G(0); and for every η > 0, for all large j, either A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅ or |π_j(y) − π_j(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_G(0). (B_s(y) = ball y s; 'for all large j' = eventually in atTop.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (xs : ℕ → Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ), IsOpen U → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → x ∈ U → (x ∈ N → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (π : Euclid P → Euclid P), 0 < δ ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 π (ball x δ) ∧ MapsTo π (ball x δ) N ∧ (∀ y ∈ N ∩ ball x δ, π y = y) ∧ ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ s ≤ δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ ball x s, ∀ z ∈ ball x s, ‖π y - π z‖ ≤ (1 + η) * ‖y - z‖) → (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto xs atTop (𝓝 x) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ G : ℝ, 0 < G → ∃ (πs : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid P) (G' : ℝ), (∀ᶠ j in atTop, dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G = ∅ ∨ (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (πs j) (ball 0 G) ∧ MapsTo (πs j) (ball 0 G) (dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G') ∧ ∀ y ∈ dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G, πs j y = y)) ∧ ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G = ∅ ∨ ∀ y ∈ ball 0 G, ∀ z ∈ ball 0 G, ‖πs j y - πs j z‖ ≤ (1 + η) * ‖y - z‖

Source: Part II.5–6 of the selected node's supplied proof (retractions onto N as in Simon 7.2.5(2), chapter-07.txt lines 166–174, rescaled for the blow-ups in the proof of 7.3.1, lines 317–337; the subsequence Cases A/B of the grandparent's proof become the disjunctions in the conclusion). No dependencies: the local retraction at x is a hypothesis, namely the conclusion of the sibling local_retraction, which the selected parent applies to N at x with d := m + 1 + ℓ when x ∈ N.
Notation: λ_j := lams j > 0, x_j := xs j, η_j := dilation x_j λ_j, so η_j(y) = −λ_j⁻¹x_j + λ_j⁻¹y = λ_j⁻¹(y − x_j); A_j := η_j(U ∩ N); B_s(y) := ball y s; a_j(z) := x_j + λ_jz. 'For all large j' means eventually in atTop. Fix G > 0.
1. (Elementary facts.) (a) η_j(a_j(z)) = λ_j⁻¹(λ_jz) = z for every z, and for every S ⊆ ℝ^P, z ∈ η_j(S) iff a_j(z) ∈ S (if z = η_j(y) then y = x_j + λ_jλ_j⁻¹(y − x_j) = a_j(z)). (b) If z ∈ B_G(0) and |x_j − x| + λ_jG ≤ t, then a_j(z) ∈ B_t(x), because |a_j(z) − x| ≤ |x_j − x| + λ_j|z| < |x_j − x| + λ_jG ≤ t. (c) For every c ∈ ℝ and t > 0, |x_j − x| + λ_jc → 0 (x_j → x, λ_j → 0), so |x_j − x| + λ_jc < t for all large j.
2. (Case A: x ∉ N.) Then x ∉ closure N, since otherwise x ∈ (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ (x ∈ U). As closure N is closed, there is r_N > 0 with B_{r_N}(x) ∩ closure N = ∅. Put π_j := id for every j and G′ := 0. By 1(c) (c := G, t := r_N), |x_j − x| + λ_jG < r_N for all large j, and for such j, A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅: if z ∈ A_j ∩ B_G(0), then u := a_j(z) ∈ U ∩ N by 1(a) and u ∈ B_{r_N}(x) by 1(b), contradicting B_{r_N}(x) ∩ N = ∅. Hence the first eventual statement holds through its first alternative, and so does the second, for every η > 0 (same eventual set of j).
3. (Case B: x ∈ N, set-up.) The hypothesis gives δ > 0 and π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with (i) π C¹ on B_δ(x), (ii) π(B_δ(x)) ⊆ N, (iii) π(y) = y for y ∈ N ∩ B_δ(x), (iv) for every η > 0 some s(η) ∈ (0, δ] with |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for y, z ∈ B_{s(η)}(x). Let s₁ := s(1) ∈ (0, δ], so π is 2-Lipschitz on B_{s₁}(x). U is open and x ∈ U: choose r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U. Define, for every j, π_j(z) := η_j(π(a_j(z))) = λ_j⁻¹(π(x_j + λ_jz) − x_j), and G′ := 5G.
4. (Case B, first statement.) By 1(c), for all large j both |x_j − x| + λ_jG < s₁ and |x_j − x| + 5λ_jG < r hold. Fix such j. By 1(b), a_j maps B_G(0) into B_{s₁}(x) ⊆ B_δ(x). If A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅, the first alternative holds. Otherwise fix z₀ ∈ A_j ∩ B_G(0); we prove the second alternative. (a) (C¹.) a_j is affine (C^∞) and maps B_G(0) into B_δ(x), where π is C¹; η_j is a constant plus the continuous linear map λ_j⁻¹·id, hence C^∞; so π_j = η_j∘π∘a_j is C¹ on B_G(0) (ContDiffOn.comp, ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn). (b) (Identity.) Let z ∈ A_j ∩ B_G(0). By 1(a), u := a_j(z) ∈ U ∩ N, and u ∈ B_δ(x) by 1(b); by (iii), π(u) = u, so π_j(z) = η_j(u) = η_j(a_j(z)) = z. (c) (Range.) w := a_j(z₀) ∈ U ∩ N by 1(a), and w ∈ B_{s₁}(x) by 1(b), so π(w) = w by (iii). Let z ∈ B_G(0) and y := a_j(z) ∈ B_{s₁}(x). Then π(y) ∈ N by (ii), and, as |z − z₀| ≤ |z| + |z₀| < 2G, |π(y) − x_j| ≤ |π(y) − π(w)| + |w − x_j| ≤ 2|y − w| + λ_j|z₀| = 2λ_j|z − z₀| + λ_j|z₀| < 4λ_jG + λ_jG = 5λ_jG. Hence |π(y) − x| ≤ |π(y) − x_j| + |x_j − x| < 5λ_jG + |x_j − x| < r, so π(y) ∈ B_r(x) ⊆ U and π(y) ∈ U ∩ N. Therefore π_j(z) = η_j(π(y)) ∈ A_j and |π_j(z)| = λ_j⁻¹|π(y) − x_j| < 5G = G′, i.e. π_j(z) ∈ A_j ∩ B_{G′}(0). Thus, for all large j, A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅, or π_j is C¹ on B_G(0), maps B_G(0) into A_j ∩ B_{G′}(0) and is the identity on A_j ∩ B_G(0).
5. (Case B, second statement.) Let η > 0 and s := s(η). By 1(c), |x_j − x| + λ_jG < s for all large j; fix such j and y, z ∈ B_G(0). By 1(b), a_j(y), a_j(z) ∈ B_s(x), and |a_j(y) − a_j(z)| = λ_j|y − z|. Since π_j(y) − π_j(z) = λ_j⁻¹(π(a_j(y)) − x_j) − λ_j⁻¹(π(a_j(z)) − x_j) = λ_j⁻¹(π(a_j(y)) − π(a_j(z))), (iv) gives |π_j(y) − π_j(z)| ≤ λ_j⁻¹(1 + η)λ_j|y − z| = (1 + η)|y − z|. So the second alternative holds for all large j.
6. (Conclusion.) In both cases the maps π_j and the radius G′ are chosen before η, and steps 2, 4 and 5 give the two eventual statements, for every G > 0. ∎

theorem Submission.dimred_mbl_bh_moving_rescaled_retractions : ∀ (P : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (xs : ℕ → Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ), IsOpen U → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → x ∈ U → (x ∈ N → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (π : Euclid P → Euclid P), 0 < δ ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 π (ball x δ) ∧ MapsTo π (ball x δ) N ∧ (∀ y ∈ N ∩ ball x δ, π y = y) ∧ ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ s ≤ δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ ball x s, ∀ z ∈ ball x s, ‖π y - π z‖ ≤ (1 + η) * ‖y - z‖) → (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto xs atTop (𝓝 x) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ G : ℝ, 0 < G → ∃ (πs : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid P) (G' : ℝ), (∀ᶠ j in atTop, dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G = ∅ ∨ (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (πs j) (ball 0 G) ∧ MapsTo (πs j) (ball 0 G) (dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G') ∧ ∀ y ∈ dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G, πs j y = y)) ∧ ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G = ∅ ∨ ∀ y ∈ ball 0 G, ∀ z ∈ ball 0 G, ‖πs j y - πs j z‖ ≤ (1 + η) * ‖y - z‖ := by
  intro P U N x xs lams hU hcl hxU hret hlams hxs hlam0 G hG
  -- `η_{a,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹ • (y - a)`
  have hdil : ∀ (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (y : Euclid P), dilation a lam y = lam⁻¹ • (y - a) := by
    intro a lam y
    simp only [dilation, dilationCLM, FunLike.coe_smul, Pi.smul_apply,
      ContinuousLinearMap.coe_id', id_eq, smul_sub]
    abel
  -- `z ∈ η_{a,λ}(S) ↔ a + λ z ∈ S`
  have hmem_img : ∀ (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P), lam ≠ 0 →
      (z ∈ dilation a lam '' S ↔ a + lam • z ∈ S) := by
    intro a lam S z hlam
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
      rwa [hdil, smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hlam, one_smul, add_sub_cancel]
    · intro h
      exact ⟨a + lam • z, h, by rw [hdil, add_sub_cancel_left, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hlam,
        one_smul]⟩
  -- `|x_j - x| + λ_j c` is eventually below any positive bound
  have hsmall : ∀ (c t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, dist (xs j) x + lams j * c < t := by
    intro c t ht
    have h1 : Tendsto (fun j => dist (xs j) x) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
      (tendsto_iff_dist_tendsto_zero).1 hxs
    have h2 : Tendsto (fun j => lams j * c) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      simpa using hlam0.mul_const c
    have h0 : Tendsto (fun j => dist (xs j) x + lams j * c) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      simpa using h1.add h2
    exact (tendsto_order.1 h0).2 t ht
  -- `x_j + λ_j z ∈ B_t(x)` for `z ∈ B_G(0)` once `|x_j - x| + λ_j G ≤ t`
  have haff : ∀ (j : ℕ) (z : Euclid P) (t : ℝ), z ∈ ball (0 : Euclid P) G →
      dist (xs j) x + lams j * G ≤ t → xs j + lams j • z ∈ ball x t := by
    intro j z t hz ht
    have hlam := hlams j
    rw [mem_ball, dist_zero_right] at hz
    rw [mem_ball]
    calc dist (xs j + lams j • z) x ≤ dist (xs j + lams j • z) (xs j) + dist (xs j) x :=
          dist_triangle _ _ _
      _ = lams j * ‖z‖ + dist (xs j) x := by
          rw [dist_eq_norm, add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg hlam.le]
      _ < lams j * G + dist (xs j) x := by
          have := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hz hlam
          linarith
      _ ≤ t := by linarith
  by_cases hxN : x ∈ N
  · -- Case B: `x ∈ N`; rescale the local retraction at `x`
    obtain ⟨δ, π, hδ, hC, hmaps, hid, hlip⟩ := hret hxN
    obtain ⟨r, hr, hrU⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.1 hU x hxU
    obtain ⟨s₁, hs₁, hs₁δ, hlip1⟩ := hlip 1 one_pos
    refine ⟨fun j z => dilation (xs j) (lams j) (π (xs j + lams j • z)), 5 * G, ?_, ?_⟩
    · filter_upwards [hsmall G s₁ hs₁, hsmall (5 * G) r hr] with j hj1 hj2
      have hlam := hlams j
      by_cases hempty : dilation (xs j) (lams j) '' (U ∩ N) ∩ ball 0 G = ∅
      · exact Or.inl hempty
      right
      obtain ⟨z₀, hz₀A, hz₀G⟩ := Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.2 hempty
      have hw : xs j + lams j • z₀ ∈ U ∩ N := (hmem_img _ _ _ _ hlam.ne').1 hz₀A
      have hwball : xs j + lams j • z₀ ∈ ball x s₁ := haff j z₀ s₁ hz₀G hj1.le
      have hπw : π (xs j + lams j • z₀) = xs j + lams j • z₀ :=
        hid _ ⟨hw.2, ball_subset_ball hs₁δ hwball⟩
      have hmapsδ : MapsTo (fun z : Euclid P => xs j + lams j • z) (ball 0 G) (ball x δ) :=
        fun z hz => ball_subset_ball hs₁δ (haff j z s₁ hz hj1.le)
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · -- `π_j` is `C¹` on `B_G(0)`
        have hdilC : ContDiff ℝ 1 (dilation (xs j) (lams j)) := by
          unfold dilation
          exact contDiff_const.add (dilationCLM P (lams j)).contDiff
        have haffC : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun z : Euclid P => xs j + lams j • z) :=
          contDiff_const.add (contDiff_id.const_smul (lams j))
        exact hdilC.comp_contDiffOn (hC.comp haffC.contDiffOn hmapsδ)
      · -- `π_j` maps `B_G(0)` into `A_j ∩ B_{5G}(0)`
        intro z hz
        have hy1 : xs j + lams j • z ∈ ball x s₁ := haff j z s₁ hz hj1.le
        have hzG : ‖z‖ < G := by simpa using hz
        have hz₀G' : ‖z₀‖ < G := by simpa using hz₀G
        have hbound : ‖π (xs j + lams j • z) - xs j‖ < 5 * (lams j * G) := by
          have hl := hlip1 _ hy1 _ hwball
